title: The Monsoon of Devil's Throat
premise: Elodie Winterbourne, a railroad engineer who maps closed lines to outrun a grief she refuses to name, is surveying the Devil's Throat coastline when an unusual tide exposes a sea cave holding the wreck of the Meridian Star — and, inside it, evidence that her grandfather's legendary salvage claim was stolen from a drowned crew he abandoned. When a ruthless salvage fleet arrives with forged papers and six tides of legal cover, Elodie must choose between the inheritance that made her family and the justice owed to the dead. Racing the fleet through collapsing tunnels and monsoon swells, she recovers the crew's true manifest and forces its confession into daylight. In the end she surrenders the gold to the descendants' trust, keeps only the map, and finally begins measuring life in years again.
about_author: Petra Amberdale is a former coastal surveyor who spent a decade charting tidal caves along forgotten shipping lanes before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels where engineering precision collides with old sins, and where the sea always keeps better records than people do.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Surveying the Devil's Throat cliffs for a decommissioned rail spur, Elodie measures everything — distances, tides, even grief — in precise units, seven years after her grandfather's funeral. A freak low tide drains a hidden cave mouth below her instruments. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness cracked open by wonder.

chapters.title: The Cave That Charges Admission
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She descends into the exposed cavern at slack water and finds the ribbed hull of the Meridian Star, sealed since 1911, plus a brass strongbox stamped with her family crest. Legends said the cave devours trespassers; instead it offers proof. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread as the tide begins returning.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Back in port, she deciphers the strongbox: her grandfather's original salvage claim, dated three days before the wreck — meaning he knew the ship would sink. Then she spots the salvage fleet's survey vessel anchoring off the Throat, flying papers that will make anything inside theirs in six tides. Emotional beat: cold clarity of a countdown beginning.

chapters.title: The Fleet at Anchor
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Marcus Vane, the fleet's salvage master, who holds forged documentation and orders to strip the site fast. Vane is no cartoon villain — he's retiring on this one haul. He notices fresh rope marks at the cave. Emotional beat: professional menace; two hunters now share one quarry.

chapters.title: What Grandfather Knew
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Digging through her late grandfather's estate, she finds his field journals: the Meridian carried striking dockworkers he'd helped blacklist, and he sold their route to pirates for the insurance and salvage rights. The 'family legend' is a confession he never finished writing. Emotional beat: identity shattered — she is heir to both crime and its evidence.

chapters.title: The Descendants' List
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The journal names eleven drowned crew members; she tracks down a living descendant, Tomas Reyes, a fisherman whose family lost everything to the scandal that followed the wreck. Skeptical, then convinced by the strongbox, Tomas agrees to help — but insists the truth go public, not just the gold. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, first warmth in seven years.

chapters.title: Monsoon Rising
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. The storm front arrives early; Vane's company lawyer warns the salvage window may close, so he moves up the operation despite dangerous seas. His diver reports the strongbox missing from the wreck. Vane deduces a rival and sets a trap at the cave mouth. Emotional beat: pressure tightening on every side.

chapters.title: The Third Tide
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Racing the storm, Elodie and Tomas dive to recover the crew's true manifest — proof of the blacklisted workers — but Vane's men seal the cave entrance behind them. Trapped as the monsoon surge floods the lower gallery, they escape through a blowhole Elodie's own survey maps predicted. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into competence; her engineering saves them.

chapters.title: Devil's Throat
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. At the height of the storm, Vane's crane barge tries to raise the wreck illegally; Elodie broadcasts the manifest and her grandfather's confession to the coast guard, press, and descendant families gathered on the cliffs. Vane cuts the cable rather than be caught, nearly capsizing; Elodie, aboard to place the evidence beacon, is nearly dragged under but survives as authorities seize the barge. Emotional beat: fury, risk, and vindication in crashing waves.

chapters.title: Years, Not Miles
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Weeks later, the gold funds a trust for the crew's descendants; Vane faces charges; her grandfather's name is rewritten in the record. Elodie donates the map to the maritime museum, keeps only his unfinished final journal page, and adds a last line in her own hand. With Tomas watching the tide come in, she stops checking her watch. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined, identity reclaimed, time finally allowed to pass.
